clauses.current_legal_basis: The order's own held text read with the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog (coverage notes read): the 10 U.S.C. 1035 note in U.S. Code release point 119-121 (current through 2026-10-09) prints the order with no ending statement; the held text of 10 U.S.C. 1035(b) (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t10-s1035.txt) still lets the President prescribe interest not exceeding 10 percent a year; the searches found no hit that ends or amends the order. clauses.reason: The command that amounts deposited under 10 U.S.C. 1035 accrue interest at ten percent per annum, compounded quarterly, is operative on 2026-10-14: no held instrument amends, revokes or supersedes it, the Code prints it as a note to section 1035, and section 1035(b) still authorizes a presidentially prescribed rate not above 10 percent a year. The September 1, 1966 sentence is a start date and not an end. The 1989 codification's editorial note about a March 28, 1973 terminal date prescribed by DOD Instruction 1348.15 is tested in the earlier-end check and is not a presidential ending of the rate command.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11298 of August 14, 1966 (31 FR 10915), Prescribing the Interest Rate for Deposit of Savings of Members of the Uniformed Services, is a single paragraph. Acting under section 1035 of title 10, United States Code, as amended by the Act of August 14, 1966, it prescribes that amounts deposited by members of the uniformed services under that section accrue interest at ten percent per annum, compounded quarterly, and states that the order is effective September 1, 1966. The held Federal Register page text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11298.txt, GPO Federal Register of August 17, 1966) carries the heading directly above the paragraph, and the order has no other paragraph. The September 1, 1966 sentence is a start date, not an end. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 11298 finds only the order's own Federal Register page and the 1989 OFR codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_11298.txt). The OFR executive-order catalog records no disposition note for the order, and the three bounded searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog; coverage notes read) report no hit that amends, revokes or supersedes it. The U.S. Code release point 119-121 (Office of the Law Revision Counsel, edition current through 2026-10-09; changes enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note to 10 U.S.C. 1035 with no ending statement. The held text of 10 U.S.C. 1035(b) (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t10-s1035.txt) provides that interest at a rate prescribed by the President, not to exceed 10 percent a year, accrues on amounts deposited under that section, so the statute the order implements remains in force and the prescribed rate equals its ceiling. The same held section text still provides special treatment for members in a missing status during the Vietnam conflict, the Persian Gulf conflict or a contingency operation, and its amendment notes record a 1991 amendment (Pub. L. 102-190, section 639(a)), so the deposit program was still being legislated after 1973. The 1989 codification prints an editorial note that on January 26, 1973 a terminal date of March 28, 1973 was prescribed by DOD Instruction 1348.15; the earlier-end check below tests that note and explains why it does not end the order. The order is operative on 2026-10-14.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states no end date, event or condition; its only date, September 1, 1966, starts it. Held texts naming EO 11298 record no revocation, supersession or amendment. The 1989 OFR codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_11298.txt, an OCR text of the Government Printing Office volume, not the original) prints an editorial note under the order that on January 26, 1973 a terminal date of March 28, 1973 was prescribed by DOD Instruction 1348.15. That Instruction is not held, and the note does not say that the President's rate prescription was revoked or amended. It records a Department of Defense issuance, an administrative act under the joint regulations that 10 U.S.C. 1035(a) assigns to the Secretaries concerned, not a presidential instrument. The held evidence does not show that the terminal date was a date for the rate command: the order itself limits nothing to a period, the held statute text has since been amended to address deposits by members during the Persian Gulf conflict and contingency operations, so a presidentially prescribed rate remained needed after March 28, 1973, and no later presidential rate prescription is held. I therefore do not treat March 28, 1973 as an end of this order. What the Instruction itself ended (deposits in the then-current program period) is not established by held sources, and that does not change the state of this command, which applies to any amounts deposited under section 1035.","independent_command_check":"There is one command. The packet inventory has one clause, EO:11298#whole, covering both, and I confirmed it complete against the held page text."}
